title: MCP transports and authorization
description: Choose local or remote transport and preserve the resource authorization boundary.
objectives: Separate token validation from permission to perform a specific action
explanation: A transport carries MCP messages without changing the purpose of tools, resources, or prompts. In the 2026-07-28 specification, stdio uses a client-launched subprocess. Streamable HTTP sends messages to an MCP endpoint and carries replies as JSON or request-scoped event streams.

The HTTP authorization specification defines an OAuth-based flow for restricted remote servers. A client discovers authorization information and obtains a token intended for the resource server. The server must validate that token appropriately. Local stdio credentials instead come from the process environment or other local configuration; do not apply the HTTP OAuth flow blindly.

Authentication identifies a caller; authorization determines what that caller may do. Apply resource-level permissions after token validation and bind consequential actions to any required approval. Never forward a received bearer token to an unrelated downstream service. Pin the protocol and SDK versions because connection and metadata rules can evolve.

terms.definition: The service protecting an API or capability.
The intended recipient or resource for a token.
A declared range of access associated with authorization.

example: A remote policy server accepts a token issued for that server, then restricts searches to the caller permitted teams. The same token is not reused as a credential for an unrelated billing API. A local demonstration uses stdio without publishing an HTTP port.
mistakes: Treating a valid token as permission for every document.
Forwarding tokens to arbitrary tool-selected destinations.
Mixing old handshake examples with a different protocol version.
exercise: Compare a local inventory tool and a remote policy server. For each, write transport, credential source, validation point, resource checks, expiry behavior, and error response. Include an expired token and wrong-audience case for the remote design.

questions.question: Does changing MCP transport change what a tool means?
questions.answer: No. Transport carries messages; capability semantics remain part of the protocol and application.
questions.distractor: Yes, every HTTP tool becomes a resource.

questions.question: What must a remote service check about an access token?
questions.answer: That it is valid for the service and the requested access, including applicable issuer, audience, expiry, and scopes.
questions.distractor: Only that the string is nonempty.

questions.question: A valid caller requests another team private document. What should happen?
questions.answer: Resource-level authorization must deny access unless the caller has the required permission.
questions.distractor: Token validity automatically authorizes every team.

questions.question: Why avoid passing an incoming token to an unrelated API?
questions.answer: It can violate audience boundaries and expose a credential to an unintended recipient.
questions.distractor: Tokens are public identifiers with no security meaning.

questions.question: Should local stdio automatically use the HTTP OAuth flow?
questions.answer: No. The specification distinguishes local process credentials from HTTP authorization.
questions.distractor: Yes, every subprocess requires a browser OAuth callback.
